The game has mocked the idea of "completing scenes and gathering affection points" enough times that I think green path is a trap. It's also the easiest one to catch someone narratively in since if you did full green, that means you did EVERY event, including the fucked up ones. You could miss a whole bunch of events or just one and be "red" though and that's a much harder nuance to account for, especially if you want to say something targeted and have to account for the specific scenes they missed. This is only reinforced by
Pareidolia trying to break Akira into being "The Collector," it's very on the nose.

That being said if we're gonna mark endings as "true" and not, I do thing green path would be most likely to lead to a "true" ending, I just don't think it'd be a very happy one. Reminds me of Paper Lily: Project Kat. There's plenty of alternate endings, even a happy one where she makes friends, but the "true" ending is that all of them die. Same with Mad Father or The Witch's House, plenty of "true" endings where awful things happen. Alternatively, red path could be a true ending in that Akira wasn't as horrible as he could've been (except this also doesn't work because you could've only missed good homie or something, but one exception is easy enough to check). It could go either way really.

Moonflare said:
This adds a lot of fuel to the theory that a red path Akira might not be able to achieve the true end due to not growing enough. I guess it could also be a jab at the players, but I can interpret the "everyone else is growing" as every other character is growing.
Click to expand...
As someone who also faithfully observes the green path and will keep doing that no matter what, I still cannot in good faith absolutely believe that this isn’t just Selly jabbing players, especially when such mockery almost only happens to players who walk on wizard-free paths and not extensively all other red paths. It’s just him taunting players who choose the option HE created.

There are two biggest problems for me about the general green = canon business: first is that not all missable events have positive meaning or result in any form of agreeable character growth; second is that there has not been an actual and major consequence for these choices yet, not even the most alarming one that is amifingered (but obviously the latter one is subject to change).

Some examples here:
- Green path Sensei has several chances to tarnish Ayane’s love for him; a few times by Kirin and one time by Chika. There is no positive meaning or character growth which I can find that otherwise wouldn’t happen on the red path. Ayane is still awesome and Sensei is still trash no matter what happened.
- The community’s favorite Stomachache. That event is GREAT. But if it’s about character growth, I’d say the Sensei that was able to refuse to resort to his usual sex method grows a hell lot more than the Sensei that continued the cycle of abuse. I imagine I’d get a lot of disapproval with that, but the point is determining what leads to a true end with something this subjective is a mess. This can be expanded to Haruka where her whole situation is a lot more negative than positive. I do all of them because it’s enticing, not that I’ve convinced myself that adultery was the only way forward for Haruka or was a good influence on her or Sensei and therefore it’s green.
- Then we have lust events that beg to have deeper meanings, especially when it involves more than one MILF at the same time. The “learning important lessons” theory can’t even be consistent among all missable events and I am not about establishing additional rulings (ex: normal events count but lust events don't; main character events count but side character events don't, etc) that make it even less believable.
- Karinlied. The only thing good about lying to Karin is a free fabulous sushi lunch/dinner, and absolutely nothing good in terms of anyone's character development is gated by this choice.

tldr: I just treat all missable events as side quests, shapable futures, and consequences; something well below canon or truth path considerations. Only events that aren’t missable are canon, and events that are missable at best impact main quests in very minor ways. What are the main quests? Save the world, slay the gods, stop the cycle, and sex our Maya (happily); the rest is just whether I want to 100% this game or not and it’s completely preferential. I’ll change my mind if one day a future update gives me an unavoidable early game over all because I didn’t jerk off in front of Tsubasa.

With only a few days until the next update, I'm finally getting around to writing up my thoughts on lore/meta-plot stuff from 0.46 - I'm nothing if not timely!

There's a brief passage in "Now & Forever" where Sensei starts to think about his childhood trauma. Personally I can only make sense of his train of thought if Nozomu raped Akira, though maybe (hopefully?) someone else has a better explanation.



The thoughts are vague enough that you could come up with an explanation where the rape is referring to Sekai and then he abruptly switches topics to Nozomu, but the reading where he's thinking about Nozomu the entire time is much more straightforward.

1. Sensei specifically uses the word rape, which he's never used to describe what Sekai did to him, neither out loud nor in his thoughts. For example, in "Stomachache" he instead phrases it as he "bloomed before he was meant to". Either he's finally come to a realization about Sekai, or he's thinking about someone else - and none of the rest of the thoughts connect to her.

2. There's a very obvious parallel in ideas: "Malvin was never raped" and "Malvin didn't have a [single] brother". This only really makes sense if the ideas "Akira was raped" and "Akira had a brother" are logically connected.

3. Thinking specifically about his brother makes Sensei start to "go insane" and try to get Imani to distract him with first conversation and then sex. Sensei has a history of avoiding confronting his trauma through the distraction of sex.

4. Nozomu is described as a "glutton" in the same way as Spork, who represents the god Nozomu/Hope aka "The Lust Eater". The implication is that Nozomu gorges himself on something sexual, and this is traumatic for Sensei.

5. Nozomu is the type to "take", implying he specifically took something from Akira. The idea "taking" something is used repeatedly in the game to describe sexual predation: taking innocence/virginity/etc. Nozomu could have "took" from someone other than Akira, but that wouldn't explain why it's traumatic for him to think about.

As Moonflare recently pointed out, Sensei is required to take something that doesn't belong to him (rape someone) because something was taken from him (he was raped).
If the thing that was taken from Akira refers to Sekai committing statutory rape and taking his virginity, then you would think that's it's enough for Sensei to do the same, but in Chapter 3 he took the virginities of Futaba and Nodoka and that wasn't sufficient to complete his homework.
"Girls Just Want to Have Fun":


"Stomachache":
Instead he needs to "take" someone unwillingly, which implies someone did the same to him. Either we've been lied to about how Sekai groomed Akira into loving her, or someone else raped Akira first.


As a side note, the identity of the [redacted] who wouldn't want to see Akira as a predator is a bit of a mystery. From context, it sounds like someone he knew in his childhood. At this point he has no problem thinking of the names of Maya (Prime), Sekai, or Saki (he even asks Miu about her in Terminal 22), so I don't think it's any of them. He never thinks of Nozomu by name, but Nozomu was probably a predator himself and at the very least a piece of shit. He has no memories of Yuu at all. So my best guess is that this is someone we don't know about yet - likely someone from Terminal 22 who never existed in Terminal 23. Possibly it's related to the girl whose name starts with the letter T and/or "Narrator Ami", but that's a subject for another (very complicated) post.
I want to stress the word possible here - I'm going to throw out a few things that don't seem to fit into the accepted story of Akira's childhood abuse. Nozomu being involved could be a way to explain them, but it's far from necessary or even the most probable explanation.


There's a story in "Something Everyone Knows and Ignores" about a man who was forced to suppress his sexuality.
It's been speculated for a long time that this could be Nozomu, given his connection to Sekai and how little we know about him. Saki was very religious and would probably react harshly to homosexuality. There's a brief passage in "Now & Forever" where Sensei starts to think about his childhood trauma. Personally I can only make sense of his train of thought if
Nozomu raped Akira

rape

HUH Noriko is seeing stuff now too? Interesting, and Maya is here in all her different "forms" too. At least nothing seemed happened that seem to leave a lasting trauma on Noriko...




Hmmm...sus. It's just now occurring to me that I might be underestimating just how important Sekai is going to be in the overall narrative. Hinting that it could be possible that things could be rewritten?


What happened to my Maya??? T_T Although I must admit, there's a certain allure to her bravado.
But I'm still sad because I know this isn't the same Maya we grew to know
Maya affection reset to 0. Sad day, Akira has totally accepted her loss at this point.


Hmm...could have some interesting ramifications if true. Some cosmic pact or curse that requires 3 beings or sacrifices of some sort perhaps? Or could easily just be here to mislead us.




More hinting towards a possibility of what I'm assuming is some sort of potential cosmic rewrite
Maybe something that made the town of Cum-on-Me end up how it is now? Perhaps a stretch, but interesting nonetheless.

Also Ami's words here actually mirrors the same words I told my dad once in a rare heart-to-heart moment with him. Fascinating to see such a familiar sentiment here...tragically she's speaking about her "dead" mother in this case.



Futaba is being transported into a delusion realm too?? What the heck is going on?
Also "You did" is making me feel even more confident in my theory that these delusional worlds are manifestations of their own inner trauma. But of course there still seems to many more pieces to the puzzle




Whoa and Futaba winds up in the room that Nodoka was fucking Akira...all the while she's snapped and seemingly figuring out some sort of secret to the the way the world works (or at least she thinks.)
December 28th again...
Nodoka's mom might have something to do with things, or at least she might've been exposed to the weird stuff happening perhaps.
So she's somehow leaving herself letters because she's started suspecting things were off awhile ago.
Always comes back to letters...boxes of letters?

posts.content_html_raw:
Uhh guys? Sana is listening...




Did a double take as well, WHAT HAPPENED TO SANA?




Weird. So not only is Yumi still noticing things are weird, but the "detentions" that old Sensei used to give her are implied to be sexual after all... Whoa. It definitely helps explain her character a lot more.
And now they're hiding in a storage shed...and Yumi's walls are slowly breaking down too. She is a beauty...



Ohhh shit. Shit. What a way to "find out" right after her talk with Touka about how she would react if she found out Akira wasn't exclusive to her. Part of me feels bad for her because I feel like she's been the most neglected during the depression arc. Poor Chika but at the same time its been right in front of your eyes the whole time, sweety.

I wonder how the confontation is going to go, will Akira get by by denying it since technically nothing is happening between him and Yumi yet and it could be brushed off as a misunderstanding? Or will he just drop the bullshit and force her to finally face the truth and his feelings?






Who is talking here...? My first thought is Sekai, but I suppose it could just be Akira waxing poetic again. OR possibly a unidentified third party?




AHHH this makes me feel like walking out on her and skipping Stomachache was worth it, I wonder what she says if Akira goes through with it here.
EDIT: I went here to check the day count before and after the Moon time skip and went on Stomachache route to see if anything changed and Io just doesn't mention anything about it at all, so these lines are exclusive to walking away from fucking her.
And now both of their feelings of him are out in the open... we will see how this ends up.



Himawari!! She definitely seems to have some sort of special connection to Ayane since this is the second time she's appearing before her to assist her now... Still haven't discarded my theories that Himawari is somehow Ayane's child or mom -.-



...Uh oh
And then wtf just happened? Was the "reset" skipped? Something about we aren't ready to see what happened here? HUH
We just appear to the next day, and Sana is nowhere to be seen or heard with no one mentioning her at all...
This is ominous.
EDIT: Ah... it's not a reset, just a 9 day timeskip huh? Very mysterious



I just found out I can put screenshots next to each other horizontally, so that's cool...
Anyways, this whole conversation of trying to convince Ami to let Niki move in was unnerving.
I knew it was a fool's errand, and now I'm worried about her intentions going forward now that she seems pissed of and aware of Niki and Akira's relationship.

Yggdrasil_Frahma said:
That's was my theory for a long time too, but I feel like Ch4 and maybe Ch3 kind of discourage that line of thinking. It's almost disconcerting reading Ch1/Ch2 again and seeing how much more pronounced the clues for this were. Like it's unimaginable in Ch4 2025 to imagine Maya facing the screen and giving Sensei a rundown on the holy trinity. Obviously, changes of seasons and changing narrators blah blah mean different focuses, but it's just so... weirdly uncompelling for me now. It's genuinely like Ch1-3 and Ch4+ Senseis are different people, which does have its fair share of allusions in the narration. Note how different Sensei's posture is in the Yasu remake of going shopping with Ami.





Consider: In that one scene in Ch3 with loli Maya, why does she say "This isn't what *I* wished for?"
Click to expand...
Hmm.

Well, by my theory logic,
Maya is just the female projection of Akira’s unconscious mind — his anima, if you want to get all Jungian. She’s his feminine ideal: adorable, loli-esque, smart as hell, highly sexual while still embodying miko purity, and of course, like him, she’s a victim of abuse.

So that scene — and the scenes where she’s denying him or (in Ch4) he’s denying her, are his own mind in conflict with itself.

Or she could be a transformed kitty. I like that idea too.

aramaug said:
With only a few days until the next update, I'm finally getting around to writing up my thoughts on lore/meta-plot stuff from 0.46 - I'm nothing if not timely!

There's a brief passage in "Now & Forever" where Sensei starts to think about his childhood trauma. Personally I can only make sense of his train of thought if Nozomu raped Akira, though maybe (hopefully?) someone else has a better explanation.
View attachment 4493039
View attachment 4492961

The thoughts are vague enough that you could come up with an explanation where the rape is referring to Sekai and then he abruptly switches topics to Nozomu, but the reading where he's thinking about Nozomu the entire time is much more straightforward.

1. Sensei specifically uses the word rape, which he's never used to describe what Sekai did to him, neither out loud nor in his thoughts. For example, in "Stomachache" he instead phrases it as he "bloomed before he was meant to". Either he's finally come to a realization about Sekai, or he's thinking about someone else - and none of the rest of the thoughts connect to her.

2. There's a very obvious parallel in ideas: "Malvin was never raped" and "Malvin didn't have a [single] brother". This only really makes sense if the ideas "Akira was raped" and "Akira had a brother" are logically connected.

3. Thinking specifically about his brother makes Sensei start to "go insane" and try to get Imani to distract him with first conversation and then sex. Sensei has a history of avoiding confronting his trauma through the distraction of sex.

4. Nozomu is described as a "glutton" in the same way as Spork, who represents the god Nozomu/Hope aka "The Lust Eater". The implication is that Nozomu gorges himself on something sexual, and this is traumatic for Sensei.

While I don't hate this idea, I'm still not really into "aspects of Akira" as it gets really confusing about what the heck the metaphor is when we see the girls interacting *without* him.

Right now, until proven very wrong, I think that memory loss is a side affect of being *aware* of the loops, and I kinda think that Nu-Maya is somehow going to end up being maybe the starting loop for the Maya we meet at the top of the game.
Click to expand...
Fair! It is all pretty confusing.

I guess I'm reacting:
  • To HOPE, Wires, and Pareidolia seeming to take over in Ch2 and Ch3 -- but in ways that feel like they're coming from inside Akira, rather than outside, driven by his assorted fears and desires.
  • To the narrators, who at various points seem to be Sensei or not, and are addressing Sensei--or not.
  • To the fact that so many of the girls seem to be embodiments of his fantasies (positive and negative).
  • To the absence of other men
  • To the claustrophobic confinement in Kumon-mi
  • To the time loops, which make no sense at all. Beach trips in winter? Christmas in summer (in the Northern Hemisphere)?
  • To the crazy resets, with their descent into dreamlike illogic, as well as their pointless puzzles and ridiculous quests.
All of those feel like someone trying (not yet successfully) to dig their way out of psychosis.

The it's-all-or-mostly-happening-in-Akira's-head hypothesis has so far managed to make the most sense to me, explaining what's going on without resorting to literal deus ex machinas playing puppetmasters from the outside.

Or dream/simulation scenarios, which I'd be really disappointed by.

It leaves open the question of how much of what we're experiencing is actually happening, and which characters are real, and which are projections, and that I think keeps the story compelling and mysterious while grounding it somewhat in reality.

But I'm always open to a better hypothesis!

With only a few days until the next update, I'm finally getting around to writing up my thoughts on lore/meta-plot stuff from 0.46 - I'm nothing if not timely!

There's a brief passage in "Now & Forever" where Sensei starts to think about his childhood trauma. Personally I can only make sense of his train of thought if Nozomu raped Akira, though maybe (hopefully?) someone else has a better explanation.
View attachment 4493039
View attachment 4492961

The thoughts are vague enough that you could come up with an explanation where the rape is referring to Sekai and then he abruptly switches topics to Nozomu, but the reading where he's thinking about Nozomu the entire time is much more straightforward.

1. Sensei specifically uses the word rape, which he's never used to describe what Sekai did to him, neither out loud nor in his thoughts. For example, in "Stomachache" he instead phrases it as he "bloomed before he was meant to". Either he's finally come to a realization about Sekai, or he's thinking about someone else - and none of the rest of the thoughts connect to her.

2. There's a very obvious parallel in ideas: "Malvin was never raped" and "Malvin didn't have a [single] brother". This only really makes sense if the ideas "Akira was raped" and "Akira had a brother" are logically connected.

3. Thinking specifically about his brother makes Sensei start to "go insane" and try to get Imani to distract him with first conversation and then sex. Sensei has a history of avoiding confronting his trauma through the distraction of sex.

4. Nozomu is described as a "glutton" in the same way as Spork, who represents the god Nozomu/Hope aka "The Lust Eater". The implication is that Nozomu gorges himself on something sexual, and this is traumatic for Sensei.

5. Nozomu is the type to "take", implying he specifically took something from Akira. The idea "taking" something is used repeatedly in the game to describe sexual predation: taking innocence/virginity/etc. Nozomu could have "took" from someone other than Akira, but that wouldn't explain why it's traumatic for him to think about.

As Moonflare recently pointed out, Sensei is required to take something that doesn't belong to him (rape someone) because something was taken from him (he was raped).
View attachment 4492967 View attachment 4492968 View attachment 4492969
If the thing that was taken from Akira refers to Sekai committing statutory rape and taking his virginity, then you would think that's it's enough for Sensei to do the same, but in Chapter 3 he took the virginities of Futaba and Nodoka and that wasn't sufficient to complete his homework.
"Girls Just Want to Have Fun":
View attachment 4492998

"Stomachache":
View attachment 4492993 View attachment 4492995 View attachment 4492997
Instead he needs to "take" someone unwillingly, which implies someone did the same to him. Either we've been lied to about how Sekai groomed Akira into loving her, or someone else raped Akira first.


As a side note, the identity of the [redacted] who wouldn't want to see Akira as a predator is a bit of a mystery. From context, it sounds like someone he knew in his childhood. At this point he has no problem thinking of the names of Maya (Prime), Sekai, or Saki (he even asks Miu about her in Terminal 22), so I don't think it's any of them. He never thinks of Nozomu by name, but Nozomu was probably a predator himself and at the very least a piece of shit. He has no memories of Yuu at all. So my best guess is that this is someone we don't know about yet - likely someone from Terminal 22 who never existed in Terminal 23. Possibly it's related to the girl whose name starts with the letter T and/or "Narrator Ami", but that's a subject for another (very complicated) post.
I want to stress the word possible here - I'm going to throw out a few things that don't seem to fit into the accepted story of Akira's childhood abuse. Nozomu being involved could be a way to explain them, but it's far from necessary or even the most probable explanation.


There's a story in "Something Everyone Knows and Ignores" about a man who was forced to suppress his sexuality.
View attachment 4493002
It's been speculated for a long time that this could be Nozomu, given his connection to Sekai and how little we know about him. Saki was very religious and would probably react harshly to homosexuality. There's some evidence that Nozomu was a predator who impregnated young girls (I personally believe he's the father of Sana and Rin), which would be the "trampling flowers". If it is about him, maybe Nozomu's parents forced him to suppress his homosexuality after discovering him doing stuff with Akira.


The opening narration of "Good Boy" is from the perspective of young Akira as he describes being abused.
View attachment 4493010
Maybe the "pain in my gut" is just a metaphorical "stomachache", but it could mean he was sodomized. This also sounds like a relationship based on fear: his abuser "plays rough", makes Akira "keep his mouth shut" and not "tell a soul", and doesn't allow him to have friends or go out and play. In contrast, his relationship with Sekai was based on "love" thanks to her grooming.
"Good Boy":
View attachment 4493052 View attachment 4493055 View attachment 4493058

"Mother's Milk":
View attachment 4493012 View attachment 4493013

In "Goodnight Moon" the narrator talks about how young Akira would lie awake trying to distract himself while dreading hearing the sound of his bedroom door opening.
View attachment 4493528
...
View attachment 4493015
At first glance this seems to be about Sekai given the references to the moon and a ghost. But there are problems.
First, this again sounds like a relationship based on fear. The narrator says that this was when Akira was young enough not to know something was wrong, before he learned what love was. But supposedly his relationship with Sekai was based on his love for her.
View attachment 4493048
Second, this happens in the period when Akira was living with his mother (Saki is the one who would have asked him to believe in God, and he reminds her of Yuu). How likely is it that Sekai would be living in the same house to be able to sneak into his room at night?
View attachment 4493026
And this is probably a stretch, but the fact that he's afraid of being "burned from the inside out" and something that gives more "comfort" than masturbation involves pain, again might point to him being sodomized.


"Episcopalis: Pickled Plums & Polyrhythmic Psalms" calls back to "Goodnight Moon" and has a bit where young Akira says that God's chosen messengers prey on children.
View attachment 4495550 View attachment 4495552
...
View attachment 4495554
This might be a generic dunk on priests, but Saki was supposedly a follower of Yasu's god and it's not clear if the Catholic Church even exists in this universe or why it would be relevant to young Akira. I wonder if Akira instead is referring to personal experience; the messengers could be Nozomu and Sekai, who hear the voice of god(s) like all good Arakawas do.
I tried to take an impartial look at the in-game evidence, but on a more conceptual level I don't really see the point of this potential plot twist either narratively or thematically. If anything, it seems like it would devalue the Sekai stuff and muddle the idea of the cycle of abuse if Sekai wasn't Akira's first abuser. But Selebus has more than earned the benefit of the doubt, so I trust that he will take this somewhere interesting if it does turn out to be true.

in addition to this

Akira's experience of being abused from both love and hate perspectives makes him a perfect predator candidate.

this is the reason why akira is so "special", why akira is "his favourite"
And the reason why "God" chose Akira as his hunter in this lolitophia he created.

At first, it might feel weird that a husband and wife were both having sexuel history with the same child.
but at the same time idea of wife curing the pain caused by husband is also interesting.

spoilers.title: Last thoughts
spoilers.html: I tried to take an impartial look at the in-game evidence, but on a more conceptual level I don't really see the point of this potential plot twist either narratively or thematically. If anything, it seems like it would devalue the Sekai stuff and muddle the idea of the cycle of abuse if Sekai wasn't Akira's first abuser. But Selebus has more than earned the benefit of the doubt, so I trust that he will take this somewhere interesting if it does turn out to be true.

Todd the chicken is gone? When did this happen? Did I ever comment on that or just ignore it? Is it back?
Wtf? Ayane keeping exact backups of his phone...

Why is he so damn insistent of making it seem like he want her to come over to his house as if it would be just the two of them in a house and not an apartment? Just tell it like it is...
I beg to differ. I am born on a neighbour countries national day, so people have said they remember my birthday because of it. I can't imagine Christmas would be that different. It's just inconvenient because of double presents nonsense.
Uh, what am I about to see...?
Wait, Todd or John?
I guess all the Yumi events are being knocked off chapter 3 already.
Air becoming tangible like hands trying to choke them, a huge clock with the infinity symbol, dark cafeteria. I don't like this.
Not every day you walk out of a dark cafeteria to find a blindfolded bunny sitting on a box with "What is "A" for?" written on it.
Man... I should have just left the Yumi stuff for when I woke up. It's way too late for this creepy nonsense.
That was an abrupt end... Guess I gotta detox myself from this now so I can sleep.

Why do you all carelessly throw around the mc's name with a grand reveal like this? I feel horrible. I expected to freakout and I guess I sorta did, but it was overshadowed by anger, which is partially my own fault, but come on...
Click to expand...
Because, unless someone wrote a reply solely to you and went out of their way to reveal Akira's name, we're on a thread to talk about the game. Spoilers are going to fly everywhere you look. Now, if it was a reply to you, I'm pretty sure it wasn't made out of malice but rather out of habit since, well, it is his name. A substantial amount of people call him Akira ever since because that's his name. It's much easier to remember to hide knowledge of a thing that happened than it is to remind yourself you can't call someone by their name all of a sudden.

Not specific to you now, but since the topic was brought up, I don't personally think anyone should go out of their way to hide spoilers, nor should it be an expectation. The community tends to do a good job of using tags right after an update to talk about the update, but other than that we mostly talk to other regulars here, and it'd be pointless to keep using spoilers to talk to people that all know what the spoilers are.

The situation of the thread is one where, even though we welcome newcomers, it's kind of showing up to a book discussion club when you haven't read the book. If someone is that adamant about not being spoiled, the only way is reading it before showing up - because it is going to happen no matter how much people might try to protect you.

Also I've been spoiling that Himawari's name is Ami forever, and even though Selebus hasn't proven me right yet, you all know I am.

I'm trying to get the rest of my 0.46 thoughts written up today because I know from experience that if I don't get it done before the next update, I never will. The subjects for this post: the monks and what's going on with Ami.
I couldn't stop laughing when I realized this: Sensei is hearing the voice of Maya Makinami (a glutton, she is) communicate solely through shouting the word "SPORK."

Explanation:
Sensei is hearing Diamond speak with Makoto's voice, and he's hearing Malvin speak with a voice that causes him pain, with Sekai being the most obvious possibility.
Sure enough, this is represented visually through the colors of the names: Diamond and Makoto are the same color, and Malvin and Sekai are the same color (#3c55fa and #96001B respectively). It's safe to assume that Spork has the voice of the character with the same color as him: Maya (#18b500).

Side note: Giuseppe, God of Clowns also has the exact same color as Maya, and the unused character "Selebus" has the same color as Sekai. Make of those what you will.
I think the monks are supposed to correspond to the trinity. Malvin pretty clearly represents Pareidolia. I'm not sure whether that's because he literally is Pareidolia using a new voice to talk to Sensei, or if he's a reflection of Pareidolia conjured up by Sensei's subconscious. (And yes, those are different things. Even if the gods originated from Akira's broken mind - I think they did - they are now autonomous entities with a real existence.)

Malvin has Pareidolia's red color and speaks with the voice of Sekai. He's a best friend that Akira imagined into existence because he was lonely. He's mischievous and encourages Akira to do naughty things, like pulling girls into dark rooms (which calls back to "Lavender's Green" in particular).

...

...

...
He wants Sensei to degrade Molly, which Sensei himself compares to Pareidolia.
And just like Pareidolia, he's a fake friend who definitely isn't Sensei's bro (sorry Moonflare).
We also got another of Pareidolia's blue screen of death "jokes" this update, probably indicating he's around.

If Malvin is Pareidolia, the other monks are probably the other gods. And Spork does seem to match up with Hope/Nozomu. He's a glutton and Hope is "The Lust Eater" who wants Sensei to "feed" him with sex. He's the youngest monk and Yasu said her god is younger than the others - plus the New Hope was just "born" during the last reset. Sensei also uses the "a glutton, he is" descriptor while thinking about Nozomu Arakawa.

It's hard for me to see the connection between Diamond and Wires, though. He has Hope's blue color rather than Wires's green. He has impaired vision, but Wires is the one who guides Sensei's vision. He's spiteful, which I don't think we've seen from Wires. One weak connection: he's a "good boy" and I'm fairly certain that Wires was the one who engineered the "Good Boy" event.

One last reason to think the monks are the gods: there used to be two but now there are three, with one there reluctantly. This is worded vaguely so that it could refer to the people in the bathroom, but I'm fairly certain it's about the monks.
A couple possibilities here:
  • There used be two gods (Wires and Pareidolia) but now there's three with the arrival of the New Hope. I'm not sure why one of them would be there reluctantly, though.
  • Wires has been reluctantly forced into joining Pareidolia and Hope as a single entity comprising three parts, which is the New Hope.
Whatever is going on with Ami, I think Pareidolia is involved.

The scene where Ami is cutting the meat ends by showing Pareidolia's smile from the trinity tree while she talks.
At the party, there's a conversation about Ami, which Sensei abruptly ends by saying she won't be coming and asking where Malvin is.

...
The same frame of Malvin flashes on the screen when Ami is confronting Niki. (Side note: the line about influencing girls clearly applies to Niki as well as Sensei. Could Ami be implying that she knows about Otoha?)
When New Maya and Ayane have their conversation they're beyond the reach of Malvin - and New Maya is finally free to talk about reset stuff away from Ami. (Also a parallel to "beyond the reach of god", another indication that Malvin is Pareidolia).

We already had a strong suspicion that Ami talks to at least one non-Sekai voice, since she yelled at them to shut up, which she wouldn't do with her mom ("You & Me Against the World"). Given Pareidolia's tendency to interject in Sensei's conversations with asshole comments, it certainly could have been him.
There's so much to talk about here that it would take a whole host of dedicated posts, but I at least want to lay out the outlines of my current thoughts.

I believe a couple of things that might come as a surprise, especially taken together:
  • The current Ami is still the real Ami (i.e. the one we started the game with).
  • The real Ami has never killed anyone and will never kill anyone.

As far as I can see it, these are the possibilities for what's going on with Ami, in the broadest terms:
  1. Ami has always been the immortal psycho who remembers everything and kills people who get in her way.
  2. At some point in time, the real Ami was abruptly replaced by the psycho, either physically or mentally.
  3. Ami's mind has been slowly corrupted over time, and we've reached the point where the psycho has taken full control.
  4. Ami's mind has been slowly corrupted over time but she's still the one in control.
  5. There's an Evil Ami and a Good Ami and which one is in control varies from scene to scene.

I reject #1 for a vast number of reasons which I may or may not post on later, but I think the quickest to convey and one of the most compelling is that Himawari made it clear that Ami isn't a killer back in Chapter 3.
"Fairytale (The End Until Tomorrow)"


"Flowerchild":
It's possible she could lie or tell a partial truth to Ayane, but she has no reason to do so as narrator.

I reject #2 because there's just too much continuity in her actions. For example if she was replaced during the beach trip it would mean that Old Ami manipulates Ayane with the idea of a threesome in "From the Heart (Red Shell)" and then New Ami happens to do the exact same thing with New Maya during the reset. In addition, there's too many gradually ramping signs of something going wrong with her mind, starting at least as early as "Heaven for Human Blood" in the first half of Chapter 2.

The other three options are plausible, but the reason that I lean toward #4 is actually the way that she acted in 0.46 itself: I just don't believe her when she talks about assaulting Maya or killing people.

...
Her threats to Niki clearly aren't calculated, they're spontaneous attempts at attempting to regain control of the conversation. To me it really reads like a teenager trying to talk up how scary they are with false claims. If this was actually the immortal psycho, would she be talking about how she's going to do these things to Niki instead of just... doing them?

Of course this opens the question of how she knows to claim these things in the first place. It seems to me like she experienced the alternate timeline events during the reset, even if she wasn't the one making the decisions. I don't yet have a satisfactory explanation for how/why that happened.

As a last point, just to be clear, even though I think the real Ami isn't the immortal psycho, it's still possible that she's known things from the start about the world and her past selves. I just don't think she remembers everything.

spoilers.title: Monks' identities
spoilers.html:
I think the monks are supposed to correspond to the trinity. Malvin pretty clearly represents Pareidolia. I'm not sure whether that's because he literally is Pareidolia using a new voice to talk to Sensei, or if he's a reflection of Pareidolia conjured up by Sensei's subconscious. (And yes, those are different things. Even if the gods originated from Akira's broken mind - I think they did - they are now autonomous entities with a real existence.)

Malvin has Pareidolia's red color and speaks with the voice of Sekai. He's a best friend that Akira imagined into existence because he was lonely. He's mischievous and encourages Akira to do naughty things, like pulling girls into dark rooms (which calls back to "Lavender's Green" in particular).

...

...

...
He wants Sensei to degrade Molly, which Sensei himself compares to Pareidolia.
And just like Pareidolia, he's a fake friend who definitely isn't Sensei's bro (sorry Moonflare).
We also got another of Pareidolia's blue screen of death "jokes" this update, probably indicating he's around.

If Malvin is Pareidolia, the other monks are probably the other gods. And Spork does seem to match up with Hope/Nozomu. He's a glutton and Hope is "The Lust Eater" who wants Sensei to "feed" him with sex. He's the youngest monk and Yasu said her god is younger than the others - plus the New Hope was just "born" during the last reset. Sensei also uses the "a glutton, he is" descriptor while thinking about Nozomu Arakawa.

It's hard for me to see the connection between Diamond and Wires, though. He has Hope's blue color rather than Wires's green. He has impaired vision, but Wires is the one who guides Sensei's vision. He's spiteful, which I don't think we've seen from Wires. One weak connection: he's a "good boy" and I'm fairly certain that Wires was the one who engineered the "Good Boy" event.

One last reason to think the monks are the gods: there used to be two but now there are three, with one there reluctantly. This is worded vaguely so that it could refer to the people in the bathroom, but I'm fairly certain it's about the monks.
A couple possibilities here:
  • There used be two gods (Wires and Pareidolia) but now there's three with the arrival of the New Hope. I'm not sure why one of them would be there reluctantly, though.
  • Wires has been reluctantly forced into joining Pareidolia and Hope as a single entity comprising three parts, which is the New Hope.

spoilers.title: Will the real Ami Arakawa please stand up
spoilers.html:
There's so much to talk about here that it would take a whole host of dedicated posts, but I at least want to lay out the outlines of my current thoughts.

I believe a couple of things that might come as a surprise, especially taken together:
  • The current Ami is still the real Ami (i.e. the one we started the game with).
  • The real Ami has never killed anyone and will never kill anyone.

As far as I can see it, these are the possibilities for what's going on with Ami, in the broadest terms:
  1. Ami has always been the immortal psycho who remembers everything and kills people who get in her way.
  2. At some point in time, the real Ami was abruptly replaced by the psycho, either physically or mentally.
  3. Ami's mind has been slowly corrupted over time, and we've reached the point where the psycho has taken full control.
  4. Ami's mind has been slowly corrupted over time but she's still the one in control.
  5. There's an Evil Ami and a Good Ami and which one is in control varies from scene to scene.

I reject #1 for a vast number of reasons which I may or may not post on later, but I think the quickest to convey and one of the most compelling is that Himawari made it clear that Ami isn't a killer back in Chapter 3.
"Fairytale (The End Until Tomorrow)"


"Flowerchild":
It's possible she could lie or tell a partial truth to Ayane, but she has no reason to do so as narrator.

I reject #2 because there's just too much continuity in her actions. For example if she was replaced during the beach trip it would mean that Old Ami manipulates Ayane with the idea of a threesome in "From the Heart (Red Shell)" and then New Ami happens to do the exact same thing with New Maya during the reset. In addition, there's too many gradually ramping signs of something going wrong with her mind, starting at least as early as "Heaven for Human Blood" in the first half of Chapter 2.

The other three options are plausible, but the reason that I lean toward #4 is actually the way that she acted in 0.46 itself: I just don't believe her when she talks about assaulting Maya or killing people.

...
Her threats to Niki clearly aren't calculated, they're spontaneous attempts at attempting to regain control of the conversation. To me it really reads like a teenager trying to talk up how scary they are with false claims. If this was actually the immortal psycho, would she be talking about how she's going to do these things to Niki instead of just... doing them?

Of course this opens the question of how she knows to claim these things in the first place. It seems to me like she experienced the alternate timeline events during the reset, even if she wasn't the one making the decisions. I don't yet have a satisfactory explanation for how/why that happened.

As a last point, just to be clear, even though I think the real Ami isn't the immortal psycho, it's still possible that she's known things from the start about the world and her past selves. I just don't think she remembers everything.

It's possible she could lie or tell a partial truth to Ayane, but she has no reason to do so as narrator.

In addition, there's too many gradually ramping signs of something going wrong with her mind, starting at least as early as "Heaven for Human Blood" in the first half of Chapter 2.
The other three options are plausible, but the reason that I lean toward #4 is actually the way that she acted in 0.46 itself: I just don't believe her when she talks about assaulting Maya or killing people.

Her threats to Niki clearly aren't calculated, they're spontaneous attempts at attempting to regain control of the conversation. To me it really reads like a teenager trying to talk up how scary they are with false claims. If this was actually the immortal psycho, would she be talking about how she's going to do these things to Niki instead of just... doing them?
Of course this opens the question of how she knows to claim these things in the first place. It seems to me like she experienced the alternate timeline events during the reset, even if she wasn't the one making the decisions. I don't yet have a satisfactory explanation for how/why that happened.
As a last point, just to be clear, even though I think the real Ami isn't the immortal psycho, it's still possible that she's known things from the start about the world and her past selves. I just don't think she remembers everything.

This line of reasoning might sound ok on paper but it presents a pretty major problem. We call him Akira because it's his name, it's normal to refer to people by their names, especially when talking to a group of people who all know that person by their name. When it comes to the broad concept of spoilers, where does the burden lie? To what length is someone expected to go for someone else? Why does the onus of responsibility fall on all others rather than the one person most in position to protect themselves? If i don't want to be spoiled by something before i've had my first swing at it, i take a proactive approach, i make sure i avoid areas i might be spoiled, i especially avoid places and group i know are going to be discussing the subject with the most up to date information, otherwise i am absolutely going to see something i wish i hadn't. Plenty of people have already said, yeah, someone deliberately going out of their way to spoil you is a dickmove, but outside of that... wtf do we expect of people? We want to talk about the game, amongst ourselves, once we're all up to date on the latest patch we speak freely here, the spoiler tag is more used to compress large posts and suppress images from making the thread jump around as they load.

If i wanted to play this game with no chance of spoilers i would not come to this thread until i was done, i would consider it just about the dumbest thing i could do, i couldn't even know the thread policy on spoilers without looking to find out if i'd be safe or not, risking getting spoiled in the process... i just can't fathom it, and to then go on an expect everyone in the thread to behave how I think they should? Jesus, what an absolute jackass i'd be to be so self involved to expect that of other people, to consider myself so important that everyone needs to put constant effort into ensuring my world remains untainted by spoilers until I'm ready to consume this or that game/book/movie/etc. The arrogance of it honestly makes my skin crawl, i could never behave that way, just imagining it is flaring my anxiety...

Perhaps we should return to talking about what we love instead of worrying about the spoiler stuff too much. Maybe it was a misunderstanding, or Void was having a shitty day and it all just spiraled or something, but whatever the case, we have new version drop tomorrow, and I wanna stay stoked instead of...whatever this is.

To that end,

I had a question on my mind for a bit: there is an event with Yasu (I forget the name) where Sensei is talking to her on the second story dorm hall, and the whole place is fucked up and falling apart. I believe she says that its what the world looks like whenever Sensei isn't around. Now, I took that to mean that perhaps the whole world is reliant on his gaze and presence to exist, kinda like how video games don't render in areas that player isn't looking at.

Now obviously, we do sometimes see events where he isn't present, but I thought maybe if the gods are aspects of him, he is aware on some level of those events.

But with the TSS events, its starting to seem like the girls really do exist even when Akira is totally not present, especially if, as mentioned recently, the gods could have started as manifestations of Akira, but took on their own life and determination at some point.

So, then, did I just totally misunderstand that Yasu scene? Because I thought it was super fascinating thinking about what she said literally.

I have received a reply from the mods.
They did not clarify on whom, if anyone, called a mod. But they did rectify that it was a mistake on the moderation's part. Therefore, no change is needed. Also, as was previously discussed earlier, and speaking for the larger community of regulars (as it was voiced previously), I reiterate that ours is a community that tries to keep a healthy and inviting thread for all.

That does not mean, however, that we will cater to any singular opinion of how things should be done. If there is a complaint, as there was one previously today/yesterday, we will seriously take a look at it as a community and decide where to go from there (if needed).

In regard to the moderation of F95, we maintain a spirit of cooperation with them whenever needed, if such is required in the future.
Current policy of the thread regarding spoilers:
On the particular case of spoilers, it is our current policy that any conversation regarding new content, close to its release date, should be tagged (as we'll see soon with 0.47).

Other than that, it is up to each one to decide what to tag or not (but please be mindful of spoilers if it's a direct reply to someone that has made known that they're playing for the first time).

Aditionally, we encourage people to use spoiler tags, to better organize and preserve the pages of the thread with reasonable amounts of shown text per post.

Lastly, these are not rules, and neither they are mine, but simply a summary of how we've taken to do things around here. No one will be punished for not following them, we simply encourage it.
As a final note, I would also personally encourage everyone to solve whatever issues may arise by talking to the regulars, as we're always trying to be welcoming.

Edit: With that, the issue has been solved. And now we can resume the peaceful and stressful wait for 0.47. Also, I'm out of reactions.

Gonna throw in my two cents cause I like participating in this thread, I usually call him Sensei if I'm not using a spoiler tag or the blurry thingy and call him Akira only in the spoiler drop down and blurry thingy. (Also yes I know it's called Inline spoiler before someone jumps on my back about it, I'm home on a porn game forum wanna be a bit childish ) The reason is simply that's just how my brain works and I expect no one else to follow or do that unless you're talking about recently released stuff then I wish your pillow is warm and soggy on both sides. I grew up subconsciously covering or tagging spoilers cause while I don't really mind them (Unless it's something media shattering or a giant twist, like someone else earlier wrote it makes me look forward on how said spoiler came to be) but I have two best friends I love to death but would get pissy at the smallest spoilers (They are a lot better now compared to a decade ago) So when I knew I was ahead of them I had to in my head edit anything I said or wrote in real time to avoid it (My go to was I give you 2 weeks for something we are all watching/ready/playing ((Again a decade ago when we were younger and had more free time)) before I starting spoiling small stuff)

I almost posted that they weren't, and he was using autopatch to just fix the problems after the fact which was dumb. But then I doublechecked. I'm not sure if he's fully thought of all the ramifications, but he has info we don't, maybe Tsubasa isn't all omnipotent inside the manor based on this.

This is unmodified. If you saw the event where you made the choice to pull the plug or take it, you see this

Complimenting / encouraging Tsukasa isn't strictly grooming her now, but it's done in the doublespeak where it could be. There is no exclusive dialogue to separate it.

Tsubasa is seemingly sending Tsukasa to bed because she's still around thanks to Akira and his visit months ago, not necessarily because she's teeing Tsukasa up for the sex observation deck
Akira is intentionally trying to make Tsukasa see him have sex because he wants to groom her. There is no outside manipulation.

This update has 20 events, and two of them are missable.

Below is the order in which I unlocked everything, other sequences are possible. I have also included where the script called for variations in dialogue:
(please mind that invite overs should be done at night by calling said character on the phone)

01 - Tsuneyo 1 - automatic on a friday.
02 - Rin 1 - automatic on a saturday.
03 - Rin 2 - linked (nude trade variation).
04 - Rin 3 - linked.
05 - Nodoka 1 - invite over (harukasex variation).
06 - Nodoka 2 - linked (amifingered variation).
07 - Nodoka 3 - linked (missable if not on amifingered path).
08 - Molly 1 - invite over.
09 - Molly 2 - invite over.
10 - Sana 1 - invite over (check her messages in her character profile, if the number isn't showing).
11 - Sana 2 - linked (amifingered variation).
12 - Haruka 1 - automatic on a wednesday (missable if harukasex is false).
13 - Haruka 2 - automatic on a thursday (harukasex variation).
14 - Chika 1 - automatic on a saturday.
15 - Io 1 - automatic on a sunday (stomachache variation).
16 - Osako 1 - automatic on a saturday.
17 - Osako 2 - linked.
18 - Io 2 - automatic on a sunday.
19 - Chika 2 - maid cafe on an afternoon.
20 - Chika 3 - linked (chinami threesome variation).
After the conclusion of their respective inviteovers, you can headpat Nodoka, Molly and Sana. Upon reaching 500 headpats, you'll unlock their pajamas for the profiles:


If cheating through URM, the safest way is to initiate the headpats, modify "session pats" to some number just below 500, like 490, and do it manually from them. That way, the outfit will unlock as if you played it.

Just mind that if you do it like this, the total number of headpats will be way under 500. If you care about that, just modify "sanapats", or whoever's, to 500 after it.

Edit: Translation to the hex from Chika 3, thanks to azkled for figuring out that it was in reverse, and providing the translation:
we will take you and teach you to survive in this strange place you've found yourself in. and while you may not immediately agree, we can assure you that we are making the right choice. each opportunity you have received to think for yourself has resulted in pain. and while pain may fuel you for the time being, there is a limit to what one person can take before turning into another. we ask that you join us in the white room. we ask that you listen. we ask that you feel. come. take it. live again.

I didn't have much issue with Rika taking her time (for the moment, we'll see if Selebus fucks this up). My reasoning is that, first, Rika's relationship with Akira is one of almost losing their relationship due to poorly conducting conversations. It'd make sense that she'd be careful on how to approach the topic.

Second, from Rika's perspective, Akira is completely unaware of it. She saw the entire conversation with Rin and Akira didn't. And Rin pushed hard to make it seem like it was the very first time anything happened, and it was all from her end. So not only would she have to conduct a conversation, she'd have to explain that she violated his privacy, deleted everything, and held that information hostage for quite some time instead of just telling him about it. Furthermore, she'd have to disclose what her daughter did and likely ruin their relationship forever (assuming he's a normal dude), when she could just keep it hidden. Lastly, this isn't a decision she is likely to make alone, she has to talk to Rie first, and that's an entire can of worms by itself.

Also, from Rika's perspective, even though Akira's class loves him, he's a functioning adult that has relationships with adult women. It is a very dumb perspective, but one that Rika repeated many times over in her comments. So it wouldn't just be confronting him like he's an enemy, it would be confronting someone she didn't really suspect of doing anything wrong, about being a pedophile. Compound that with how their relationship isn't all that solid, and how she's the odd one out of the one group that accepted her, and yeah, that's not an easy topic.

We know Akira, but were he a normal person, I can definitely see how someone coming up to him and accusing him of being a pedophile would be more than enough for cutting ties with said person. That's not really a harmless accusation to make, especially to a teacher/former teacher.

My one gripe with this is that the situation is kind of nonsense. Akira leaves his phone behind? When did that ever happen? Then Rika is able to unlock it without knowing the password, and only sees the specific messages Rin sends then, and not everything else that is there that would incriminate him immediately? Even though she's still with the cellphone many hours later? Yeah, that's super bullshit.

Noriko and Kirin trying to figure out which dorms would have threesomes with him and right now, they are the only one even remotely close. It's not even a competition.

Getting to see where Yuki lives and yeah, it's not the prettiest place. The couch looks cozy enough.

Maybe not fall apart with Sensei but...

And here comes Imani. That shock at finding him outside. This conversation is not going the way I expected.
Oh yeah, I think Yuki and Rika could get along in a weird way. And I guess it would kind of explain that one picture (canon or not) that I saw some while ago. Which tells you absolutely nothing.

I don't even remember when i stopped being afraid of the dark.

Wonder why he imagined mystery girl as the non Chika employee.
Damn mc! You didn't have to do Uta like that!

Yup, there it is. Noriko getting upset her sister beat her to the sex thing...

Feeling obligated to write something and recount the story, maybe to freshen people memory up? I don't really know. I just feel empty if I don't say SOMETHING at least. Maya? A tsundere? Nooo... that can't be, can it? Impossible.
This looks like the perfect background for a kiss, doesn't it?
Apparently not.
Excuse me? "Maya's affection has increased by 100!"
"Hook" has only just started and I already hate it. And that's just a straight up still image jumpscare.
I hope it's a bonus cg. That would be nice. Maybe one that involves Haruka AND Molly.
I kinda wish I had a few thousand hours in WoW just to understand Molly's references. But I don't so I'm completely clueless. Same with every other game that assumes everyone and their grandma has played WoW since release.
Oh wow... Haruka has some spicy dreams about... Tsuneyo of all people?
Wtf is that option? "Rape her"?
And that lead to him walking out on her? Come on dude... It's almost like she's the one pursuing him at this point and he doesn't want to become of fear of what he did.
I don't fucking understand how he can go and kiss Yumi and still pursue her without feeling that bad about it and Yumi tries to avoid him and is very upset about what happened. But when it happens to Molly and he only sees the aftermath of it when she wasn't even conscious for the thing and she actively pursues him, then he is suddenly doing a 180 and doesn't want to further their relationship. I don't fucking get it, I just don't. And all that is happening while his pursuing other girls perfectly fine. Like fuck sake dude, the writing confuses me so much sometimes!
I feel like Molly's story is turning out to be one I dislike the most at this point.
(also doesn't help that her story entails D&D which I'm just not interested in at all)
Imagine if complaining by writing something down elsewhere somehow magically changed the story you are reading. That would be lovely. Any story tailored specifically for you by some magical process.
I feel like Molly and his relationship is still stuck in midway through chapter 2 and it's weirding me out.
She's practically BEGGING for this relationship to move forward. Like I kinda see what's going on here. She's suppose to be that character that wants him but for some reason he doesn't want her, because of trauma or whatever. And that he apparently sees bad things when he looks at her. But the execution just feels poor to me. I know I'm dragging on these complaints a bit too much but come on... can you blame me for being upset?
Tricked the mc into believing she was dressed and he still goes back to covering his vision. Made me chuckle a little contrary to belief.
Ah yes. The cliche train scene where a sudden movement pushes a male character into a female one and they end up in a compromising position.
I bet this is another replay. Just as unexciting as many others.
OMG, no fucking way dude! HAHAHAHA! Molly runs into Wakana holding that dildosaber with a blindfolded Osako.
Poor Osako doesn't even know who it was... That's probably for the better.
I can't get over the absurdity of this situation! It's so weird and funny!
Well, at least Molly is having a glorious time... My god...
That replay turned out better than expected.

posts.content_html_raw:
Finally finished the update, and... wow. A lot to unpack this time. Let's get into it:

Sorry if things feel a bit scattered. There's a lot for me to get out there.

Tenchou Tojo. So that's his name... Verrry interesting, and certainly not a reveal I expected at all, let alone at the start of the update.



Yeah, soooo... does anyone remember this post I made about us potentially still being trapped in an artificial, alternate reality of Kumon-mi that all started with the previous Beach update?

Fire Lord Zuko said:
Regarding everyone acting so chill about Akira fucking different people: I for one am not surprised in the slightest. Why? Because something is currently amiss; something different than what has happened before. We're even warned about it not once, but twice:
Click to expand...
I still believe in it wholeheartedly. Like wtf even was this exchange? Does this really sound like something Futaba would say? Timid, self-conscious Futaba? Would she seriously urge Rin to straight up fuck Akira so bluntly? I'm skeptical. If the reality itself isn't artificial, then the girls' behaviors have been altered for sure.

Something's weird, y'all. It's only a matter of time until we find out for sure.

Ohhhhhh shit. It's honestly very jarring to see Rika so serious like that, but I definitely understand her reaction. How convenient that Akira chose that moment to forget his phone. Like... goddammit! We were this close to sexing Rin! Why must you continue to blueball us, Selebus?? Is the Rin curse on par with Noriko at this point? Because I think an argument could be made.

The drama was great, though. So kudos, Sel. Ya hardly disappoint.

It was fine... Felt a bit off, though, which I suppose was the point. So my thoughts were a bit like Rin's for this one. I want to feel happy for Rin for at least getting frisky with the girl she's admired for so many years, but I honestly can't, because Chika is just blanketed in delusional choices and unwavering pain. I feel really bad for her... She deserves so much better.

But more on Chika later.



...Score one for the Simulation theory? Assuming Matsubara is Wakana's 'real' surname outside of this hypothetical simulation.

Ohhhh, Nodoka... What hasn't been said about her at this point? She is just...

Well, let's just say she never ceases to amaze me. I look forward to every time she's on screen at this point because I always wonder what she's plotting and what actions she will take to achieve her primary ambitions.

Take this for example: Nodoka casually trying to hint at Himawari's existence and no doubt planting a seed in Akira's mind so he can remember her.



Hmmmm... Himawari's skirt on the floor in the background. Nodoka emphasizing the word 'Dad'... And who was it that did 'cosplay' again?



I have to admit, the whole 'Ami Junior' persona that Nodoka adopted while 'cosplaying' and dropping hints at Himawari does seem to strengthen Moonflare's 'Himawari is named Ami' theory a bit further lol.

Oh yeah, and speaking of which, here's another hint Nodoka tries to slip in about Himawari to Akira.



Right in front of Ami Prime, too... You've got guts, Nodoka, I'll give you that.

Oh yeah, and the Ami/Nodoka threesome was pretty hot btw. By far my favorite h-scene of the update.

Okay, this exchange got a smile out of me:



I saw the posts that called Molly the 'worst written' of the main cast, but honestly, I have to disagree. I find her nerdiness very endearing and I think it's cute how she's trying to get Akira back into some of the otaku stuff from his past that made him happy. He needs to find a hobby or an outlet that isn't just sex if he's ever going to recover. But more on that topic when I discuss Osako's events.

I hope Akira trying out DnD is a thing that carries over, because him participating in a campaign is something I would very much like to witness.

First off, love this reaction:



Secondly, omg it's adult Sana from Times New Roman, what??



I can't say that was on my bingo card for this update, but this was really cool to see.

Akira once again confessed his love to yet another girl, and... well, as he said, he's been tossing the word around like candy at this point. I believe that it makes sense, though. His perception of love is just... so skewed at this point that he just doesn't know how to interpret it. It's a foreign concept to him, one he probably wants to explore, but he doesn't have a map. So he always gets lost.

The h-scene with Sana was meh. I liked the dialogue, but what dragged it down for me was the fact we couldn't even really see any of the actual fucking. It just focused on one or two angles the whole time and that was it. Such a shame... It was great to see Sana's cyclops look again, though.

Oh yeah, and Akira came inside of her apparently. Here's hoping she doesn't follow in her mom's footsteps! XD Did Sana ever get a morning after pill? I don't think that was ever addressed.

I don't really have a lot to say about Haruka's events. They were serviceable and about what I expected. It's just set-up for when Rin finally does stuff with Akira, I think. Maybe for a potential threesome? Who knows.

Also, hooray! The cafe is open once again.

Io and Yasu saw each other when they were Wizards?? Did not expect that either!

Guys, lemme tell ya. I hate Yasu's mother. Okay? Like, she sucks. But Io's mother? Oh my Goooood she pissed me off. Like, it's unreal how cruel she was to Io for literally no reason at all.



Yes, you're correct. Clearly you aren't. The irony is staggering.



Omfg Akira, thank you! Finally you make the correct decision and deliver a firm 'no'.



And this is why the Green Path is the canon path... Maybe the green choice can be a miserable one in the short term, but in the long term, you never get to witness growth such as this.

The amusement park event started out really wholesome. I'm just bummed Akira wasn't there. I've always wanted to see him take Io to the amusement park like she always wanted. Imagine it! Akira, Io and Uta at the amusement park together, getting up to a bunch of shenanigans and maybe bumping into the Takoyaki Guy again. XD That would've been a fun event. Even still, though, it was great to see two best friends hanging out together.

I still won't lose hope in the eventual Dorm 7 throuple! It's too enticing of an idea to not explore one day.

As for the latter half of the event... oooooh man. I don't think my protective instincts have flared up so much in quite awhile. Those two NPCs were creepy asf... I'm glad Yuki showed up and dealt with them.

Still... Yuki's not looking too good these days, huh? I worry for her physical health and how it will impact not only her, but also Yumi and Kaori when they discover something's wrong.

Yumi discovering her mom relapsed is deeefinitely a drama that's bound to show up later, and it won't be pretty when it does.

I used to not like Osako, and I don't think many others did either. But I gotta say... much like Otoha, Osako is really growing on me lately. I dig her friendship with Akira a lot and honestly am really invested in where her journey of self-discovery will take her.

Seeing Noriko and Kirin at the Witchcraft class was a welcome surprise. Of course Kirin would try to create a love potion. I've said it before and I'll say it again: Noriko is an angel and must be protected at all costs.

I also mentioned earlier how Akira needs to find a new hobby or... needs to make a change in his life so that he'll best be able to focus on things besides constant unhealthy sex, and really, like Noriko mentioned, I believe his friendship with Osako is the perfect way to get started on that. They're both lost and confused right now, and this is the perfect way to see them both bond.

I'm on the fence about Akira quitting teaching at school. On the one hand, I'd miss that aspect of his character, but on the other hand, seeing him do something new opens a lot of different possibilities. Wakana definitely wouldn't take that well, but we'll see where it leads.

Also, I guess Osako knows that Akira is a predator now... No more speculation on whether or not she's aware, because the confession at the bar sealed the deal. I don't have any deep insight on this particular detail, but all I know is it'll be interesting to see how Osako reacts to certain things from now on. Things that Imani and (presumably) Wakana don't even know.

Rika is undoubtedly suspicious after the Rin stuff, though. As she should be. She also has events in 0.48, so I believe we'll get to see how she responds veeery soon.

But yeah. Osako is growing on me lately. I genuinely look forward to how her story progresses.

What can I say? It's just sad all around to witness the state she's in these days... She wants so much for her new family to not fall apart that she deludes herself. I can't blame her for it, either. It really is all Akira's fault.

They both talked to each other after leaving the Maid Cafe, but it didn't really go anywhere. I mean, like one of the narrators said afterwards: one talk just isn't enough to fix everything.

I really hope Rin can act as an anchor for her in this difficult time, if only a little bit. But hey, if nothing else, Chika's TSS experience is sure to have changed her a bit, right?

...That was such a weird ending tbh. With blonde Chika returning home and Chinami looking like... whatever the hell that mannequin looking thing was. Very jarring.

I think that about sums up most of my initial thoughts. I haven't read anyone else's posts yet, so I think I'll go do that now.

But more on Chika later.



...Score one for the Simulation theory? Assuming Matsubara is Wakana's 'real' surname outside of this hypothetical simulation.

Ohhhh, Nodoka... What hasn't been said about her at this point? She is just...

Well, let's just say she never ceases to amaze me. I look forward to every time she's on screen at this point because I always wonder what she's plotting and what actions she will take to achieve her primary ambitions.

Take this for example: Nodoka casually trying to hint at Himawari's existence and no doubt planting a seed in Akira's mind so he can remember her.



Hmmmm... Himawari's skirt on the floor in the background. Nodoka emphasizing the word 'Dad'... And who was it that did 'cosplay' again?



I have to admit, the whole 'Ami Junior' persona that Nodoka adopted while 'cosplaying' and dropping hints at Himawari does seem to strengthen Moonflare's 'Himawari is named Ami' theory a bit further lol.

Oh yeah, and speaking of which, here's another hint Nodoka tries to slip in about Himawari to Akira.



Right in front of Ami Prime, too... You've got guts, Nodoka, I'll give you that.

Oh yeah, and the Ami/Nodoka threesome was pretty hot btw. By far my favorite h-scene of the update.

Okay, this exchange got a smile out of me:



I saw the posts that called Molly the 'worst written' of the main cast, but honestly, I have to disagree. I find her nerdiness very endearing and I think it's cute how she's trying to get Akira back into some of the otaku stuff from his past that made him happy. He needs to find a hobby or an outlet that isn't just sex if he's ever going to recover. But more on that topic when I discuss Osako's events.

I hope Akira trying out DnD is a thing that carries over, because him participating in a campaign is something I would very much like to witness.

First off, love this reaction:



Secondly, omg it's adult Sana from Times New Roman, what??



I can't say that was on my bingo card for this update, but this was really cool to see.

Akira once again confessed his love to yet another girl, and... well, as he said, he's been tossing the word around like candy at this point. I believe that it makes sense, though. His perception of love is just... so skewed at this point that he just doesn't know how to interpret it. It's a foreign concept to him, one he probably wants to explore, but he doesn't have a map. So he always gets lost.

The h-scene with Sana was meh. I liked the dialogue, but what dragged it down for me was the fact we couldn't even really see any of the actual fucking. It just focused on one or two angles the whole time and that was it. Such a shame... It was great to see Sana's cyclops look again, though.

Oh yeah, and Akira came inside of her apparently. Here's hoping she doesn't follow in her mom's footsteps! XD Did Sana ever get a morning after pill? I don't think that was ever addressed.

I don't really have a lot to say about Haruka's events. They were serviceable and about what I expected. It's just set-up for when Rin finally does stuff with Akira, I think. Maybe for a potential threesome? Who knows.

Also, hooray! The cafe is open once again.

Io and Yasu saw each other when they were Wizards?? Did not expect that either!

Guys, lemme tell ya. I hate Yasu's mother. Okay? Like, she sucks. But Io's mother? Oh my Goooood she pissed me off. Like, it's unreal how cruel she was to Io for literally no reason at all.



Yes, you're correct. Clearly you aren't. The irony is staggering.



Omfg Akira, thank you! Finally you make the correct decision and deliver a firm 'no'.



And this is why the Green Path is the canon path... Maybe the green choice can be a miserable one in the short term, but in the long term, you never get to witness growth such as this.

The amusement park event started out really wholesome. I'm just bummed Akira wasn't there. I've always wanted to see him take Io to the amusement park like she always wanted. Imagine it! Akira, Io and Uta at the amusement park together, getting up to a bunch of shenanigans and maybe bumping into the Takoyaki Guy again. XD That would've been a fun event. Even still, though, it was great to see two best friends hanging out together.

I still won't lose hope in the eventual Dorm 7 throuple! It's too enticing of an idea to not explore one day.

As for the latter half of the event... oooooh man. I don't think my protective instincts have flared up so much in quite awhile. Those two NPCs were creepy asf... I'm glad Yuki showed up and dealt with them.

Still... Yuki's not looking too good these days, huh? I worry for her physical health and how it will impact not only her, but also Yumi and Kaori when they discover something's wrong.

Yumi discovering her mom relapsed is deeefinitely a drama that's bound to show up later, and it won't be pretty when it does.

I used to not like Osako, and I don't think many others did either. But I gotta say... much like Otoha, Osako is really growing on me lately. I dig her friendship with Akira a lot and honestly am really invested in where her journey of self-discovery will take her.

Seeing Noriko and Kirin at the Witchcraft class was a welcome surprise. Of course Kirin would try to create a love potion. I've said it before and I'll say it again: Noriko is an angel and must be protected at all costs.

I also mentioned earlier how Akira needs to find a new hobby or... needs to make a change in his life so that he'll best be able to focus on things besides constant unhealthy sex, and really, like Noriko mentioned, I believe his friendship with Osako is the perfect way to get started on that. They're both lost and confused right now, and this is the perfect way to see them both bond.

I'm on the fence about Akira quitting teaching at school. On the one hand, I'd miss that aspect of his character, but on the other hand, seeing him do something new opens a lot of different possibilities. Wakana definitely wouldn't take that well, but we'll see where it leads.

Also, I guess Osako knows that Akira is a predator now... No more speculation on whether or not she's aware, because the confession at the bar sealed the deal. I don't have any deep insight on this particular detail, but all I know is it'll be interesting to see how Osako reacts to certain things from now on. Things that Imani and (presumably) Wakana don't even know.

Rika is undoubtedly suspicious after the Rin stuff, though. As she should be. She also has events in 0.48, so I believe we'll get to see how she responds veeery soon.

But yeah. Osako is growing on me lately. I genuinely look forward to how her story progresses.

What can I say? It's just sad all around to witness the state she's in these days... She wants so much for her new family to not fall apart that she deludes herself. I can't blame her for it, either. It really is all Akira's fault.

They both talked to each other after leaving the Maid Cafe, but it didn't really go anywhere. I mean, like one of the narrators said afterwards: one talk just isn't enough to fix everything.

I really hope Rin can act as an anchor for her in this difficult time, if only a little bit. But hey, if nothing else, Chika's TSS experience is sure to have changed her a bit, right?

...That was such a weird ending tbh. With blonde Chika returning home and Chinami looking like... whatever the hell that mannequin looking thing was. Very jarring.

I think that about sums up most of my initial thoughts. I haven't read anyone else's posts yet, so I think I'll go do that now.
